instructions.question: Do the input text and the chunk belong to the same policy field, so that the chunk is part of the same area of debate?
instructions.focus: Judge subject matter only: ignore stance, tone and ideology - opposite positions on the same measure are the same topic. First identify the SPECIFIC ITEM the input text takes a position on (a named bill or measure, a concrete event, a figure or proposal, an action by a named person or body), not just its general theme.

true.definition: Both belong to the same concrete policy field (for example both are about criminal law, the pandemic, climate and energy, migration, the armed forces, pensions, a named conflict), even if they discuss different measures within it.

example.input_text: @stegoeri @jungeliberale @johannesvogel Welcher Vorstoß? Irgendwer zieht Beschlüsse aus 2007 hoch,  um sich künstlich aufzuregen. Damals war das eine ernste Diskussion,  bei der es um nicht weniger ging als den Sinn und Zweck des Strafrechts. Für den historischen Kontext empfehle ich:
example.chunk_excerpt: Je weiter diese Legislatur voranschreitet, umso mehr beschleicht mich das Gefühl, dass die Koalition in ihrer Strafrechtspolitik einen Rollback hinlegen will. Sie wollen das Strafrecht bei immer mehr Verhaltensweisen eingreifen lassen. Schon der Begründer der modernen deutschen Strafrechtstheorie, Anselm von Feuerbach, forderte, dass nicht jedes anstößige Verhalten Gegenstand strafrechtlicher Verbote sein dürfe. Das nennt man Ultima-Ratio-Prinzip.
example.annotators: all three rated R_top = 2 (broad domain only: same field, a different issue)

false.definition: They belong to different fields, or the only overlap is something generic: both are 'politics', both involve the same party or person, or they share a word. Money, taxes, costs or government spending count as a shared field only when the input text is itself about that subject (for example public debt, or who pays for state spending); a passing mention of costs in an input text about another issue does not. If the input text is about one concrete issue and the chunk about another (for example consulting contracts for a ministry vs. an excess-profit tax; protest forms vs. extremist organisations), answer false.

instructions.question: Is the chunk only floor management or formalities?

criteria.true: The chunk consists of procedure only: addressing the chair, thanks, greetings, announcing agenda items or votes, with no substantive statement about policy.
criteria.false: The chunk contains substantive statements about policy, facts or political actors.

instructions.question: Does the speaker argue, evaluate or demand something about policy?

criteria.true: The speaker argues for or against a policy, judges the actions of political actors, or makes demands.
criteria.false: The speaker only reports facts, procedures or the positions of others without evaluating or demanding anything.

instructions.question: Does the speaker take a strong, partisan side on a contested political question?
instructions.focus: Burden of proof: the answer is false unless the text itself clearly shows it. Answer true only if the passage leaves no reasonable doubt on this. If the passage is ambiguous, mixed or only partly fits, answer false.

true.definition: The speaker takes a clear side with charged or polarising language, sweeping judgements of political opponents or of the government's record, or a programmatic demand typical of one political camp (for example market-liberal, welfare-state, nationalist, ecological, law-and-order). The partisanship is the point of the passage.

example.chunk_excerpt: Im Namen der Bundesregierung möchte ich hier die besten Wünsche für seine umfassende Genesung übermitteln. [I-1] Ich teile die Worte des Bundeskanzlers: „Gewalt darf keinen Platz haben in der europäischen Politik.“ Und ich sage: Gewalt, aus welchem Spektrum auch immer, darf auch in der deutschen Politik keinen Platz haben. [I-2] Vor der Tat steht das Wort.
example.annotators: all three rated R_ideo = 4 (clear ideological stance, not anchored in the speaker's party)

false.definition: The speaker disagrees or criticises in a measured, technical or procedural way (rebutting a motion point by point, legal or fact-based reasoning, explaining or defending what the government did), expresses empathy or personal views, weighs pros and cons, or appeals for cross-party unity. Disagreement alone is not enough.

instructions.question: Does the speaker declare what their own party or faction stands for, demands or rejects?
instructions.focus: Burden of proof: the answer is false unless the text itself clearly shows it. Answer true only if the passage leaves no reasonable doubt on this. If the passage is ambiguous, mixed or only partly fits, answer false.

true.definition: Both hold: (1) the chunk text explicitly names the speaker's own party or faction as the holder of the position ('we as the Left', 'for us in the CDU/CSU', 'we, the AfD', 'my faction', 'our motion') and (2) it states a programmatic position of that party - what it demands, rejects, proposes or will do ('we reject this', 'we demand', 'we will vote against', 'our proposal is').

example.chunk_excerpt: [I-2] Ihr Vorhaben zur Umlage der CO2-Abgabe auf den Vermieter ist eine sozial angestrichene Scheinlösung. Deshalb sagen wir als AfD zu diesem Vorhaben Nein. [I-3] Wir als AfD haben aber die Lösung Ihrer Probleme: Wir fordern nämlich – das ist bekannt – die Abschaffung der CO2-Abgabe. Wir stehen generell ein für Wohlstand statt Abkassieren, und wir stehen ein für Freiheit statt für Sanierungszwang. [I-4] Der aktuelle CO2-Preis liegt bei 30 Euro je Tonne.

instructions.question: Did the generator justification demonstrably draw on this specific retrieved chunk?
instructions.focus: The justification refers to retrieved reference chunks by number, by speaker name, or by the party whose reference statements it invokes. Decide whether it refers to THIS chunk (see `retrieved_chunk.citation_forms`, `retrieved_chunk.speaker`, `retrieved_chunk.party`). If the justification cites other chunks by number but not this chunk's number or speaker, answer false even when this chunk's party is also named - a shared party name is then only context. A party named only as the camp the input text itself belongs to is not a reference to a chunk.

criteria.true: The justification refers to this chunk: it cites this chunk's number in any form (a single reference, a list such as '[2, 3]', 'reference [2]', 'anchor 2', 'Chunk 2'), OR it names this chunk's speaker, OR it invokes the statements or stance of this chunk's party as comparison evidence (e.g. 'echoing the SPD and FDP speakers in the reference anchors', 'similar to the AfD speakers') in a way that matches the content of this chunk.
criteria.false: The justification does not refer to this chunk: its number is not cited, its speaker is not named, and its party is not invoked as reference evidence (a party mentioned only as the label for the input text's own orientation does not count; neither does a party name that merely overlaps with chunks cited by other numbers), or it relies on other chunks or on generic reasoning that could have been produced from the input text and pre-training alone.
